::: {#rem-church-turing}
#### The Church-Turing thesis

Every model of computation that has been proposed and that can be built,
from programming languages to random-access machines,
can be simulated by a [Turing machine](#def-turing-machine).
The *Church-Turing thesis* claims that every function a physical device can compute,
a Turing machine can compute.
It is a claim about the physical world, not a theorem.
A stronger version, which quantum computers may refute,
says the simulation costs at most a polynomial increase in [running time](p-and-np.qmd#def-running-time)
[@arora2009computational, section 1.6].
Under that version, [the class P](p-and-np.qmd#def-class-p) is the same
whichever reasonable model it is defined with,
as @thm-tm-robustness shows for the variations of the Turing machine itself.

:::
